P1-05.P1_flat: - Forwarded transactions. A bus transaction (a request or response with its address, data and handshake) that the unit only forwards between its ports or to a sub-unit, without storing, computing or deciding it, is not a conceptual asset of this unit; this rule, its sentences on relayed data included, never covers a bus whose address this unit drives on a non-record output port of its own and whose acknowledge it takes on a non-record input port of its own (judge from port names which ports are that bus's address, acknowledge and other lines, and say so): the request it drives onto that bus's ports and the response it takes from them are judged as usual, as information leaving and entering the unit there. Also forwarding: merging several ports' bus responses into one (an OR or a multiplexer); a register stage passing a whole request or response record on unchanged a cycle later, although it stores the record; and a record this unit only wires between one of its ports and the port map of an instance of another IP, with no statement of this unit reading or writing it (a constant tied to it in a generate branch lacking the instance is no such statement), even though the black-box rule lets the instance change it. The decision whether or where it passes is judged as usual. Relayed data is data a transfer carries into or out of the unit (data loaded or stored, instruction words fetched, messages received or sent) when no statement of this unit stores it or computes from it and it only moves between unit ports, between a unit port and an instance of another IP, between such instances, through a register stage, or into a statement only mixing it with other values (an OR, a multiplexer). Relayed data, alone or with only the acknowledge and ready lines timing its transfer, is not a piece of its own, even in a unit executing instructions and although step 1 names data received or returned and 4.2 end-user's private data: keep no concept for it. Judged as usual by this rule only: a transfer's address and direction; a wait or fault flag; an interrupt or debug request; a register read-back word, and the register contents an instance other than a buffer or register stage holds; an arithmetic, logic or compare result an instance computes from operands; the value a mixing statement writes (such as the value written back to a register), unless that statement mixes only relayed data, bus responses and constants; and data the unit stores (not a register stage's copy), shifts through its own register, generates or computes from, even when a buffer instance also holds it. Judge from port names which instance ports carry relayed data and which a computed result, and say so.
P1-05.P1_structured:
- Forwarded transactions (a).
  Scope: A bus transaction (a request or response with its address, data and handshake).
  Criteria (any of): (1) that the unit only forwards between its ports or to a sub-unit, without storing, computing or deciding it; also forwarding: (2) merging several ports' bus responses into one (an OR or a multiplexer); (3) a register stage passing a whole request or response record on unchanged a cycle later, although it stores the record; (4) a record this unit only wires between one of its ports and the port map of an instance of another IP, with no statement of this unit reading or writing it (a constant tied to it in a generate branch lacking the instance is no such statement), even though the black-box rule lets the instance change it.
  Exceptions: a bus whose address this unit drives on a non-record output port of its own and whose acknowledge it takes on a non-record input port of its own: the request it drives onto that bus's ports and the response it takes from them are judged as usual, as information leaving and entering the unit there; the decision whether or where the transaction passes; a transfer's address and direction; a wait or fault flag; an interrupt or debug request; a register read-back word, and the register contents an instance other than a buffer or register stage holds; an arithmetic, logic or compare result an instance computes from operands; the value a mixing statement writes (such as the value written back to a register), unless that statement mixes only relayed data, bus responses and constants; and data the unit stores (not a register stage's copy), shifts through its own register, generates or computes from, even when a buffer instance also holds it.
  Outcome: is not a conceptual asset of this unit.
  Evidence: judge from port names which ports are that bus's address, acknowledge and other lines, and say so.
- Forwarded transactions (b).
  Scope: Relayed data is data a transfer carries into or out of the unit (data loaded or stored, instruction words fetched, messages received or sent).
  Criteria: (1) no statement of this unit stores it or computes from it; (2) it only moves between unit ports, between a unit port and an instance of another IP, between such instances, through a register stage, or into a statement only mixing it with other values (an OR, a multiplexer).
  Exceptions: those of (a).
  Outcome: Relayed data, alone or with only the acknowledge and ready lines timing its transfer, is not a piece of its own, even in a unit executing instructions and although step 1 names data received or returned and 4.2 end-user's private data: keep no concept for it.
  Evidence: Judge from port names which instance ports carry relayed data and which a computed result, and say so.
P1-05.P2_flat: An internal array whose elements, one per port, this unit sets each to a whole bus request or response record (2.6) copied from one record or a constant, never qualifies for any conceptual asset: it only passes the transaction on, and a select or compare gating an element's strobe only decides that field (2.2) or mixes into it (2.6), so the decision stays where it is computed. A select computed from that compare (such as a bit-per-port vector) is the decision's own element and stays its primary. If the compare is inline in a condition, the decision has no element of its own and adds no primary, even when the held lines assign the array; do not move the primary to the record the array copies or its fields, which only feed the compare or carry the transaction. A single strobe, enable or request flag a decision gates is judged as usual. A record this unit only wires between a unit port and the port map of an instance of another IP, with no statement of this unit reading or writing it or its fields (a constant tied to it in a generate branch lacking the instance is no such statement), never qualifies for any conceptual asset, nor do its fields: the instance holds the value; the record only carries it. Judged as usual: a record this unit's statements read or write, a non-record port even if wired straight into an instance, and an element of this unit deciding whether or where the record passes. Relayed data is data a transfer carries into or out of the unit (data loaded or stored, instruction words fetched, messages received or sent) when no statement of this unit stores it or computes from it and it only moves between unit ports, between a unit port and an instance of another IP, between such instances, through a register stage, or into a statement only mixing it with other values (an OR, a multiplexer). No element qualifies as primary for a conceptual asset about relayed data, alone or with only the acknowledge and ready lines timing its transfer, even in a unit executing instructions and where 4.2 points at it: Phase 1 does not keep such a concept, so it has no secondary (step 5); under other conceptual assets its elements keep their usual labels. Judged as usual: a transfer's address and direction; a wait or fault flag; an interrupt or debug request; a register read-back word, and the register contents an instance other than a buffer or register stage holds; an arithmetic, logic or compare result an instance computes; the value a mixing statement writes (such as the value written back to a register), unless that statement mixes only relayed data, bus responses and constants; and data the unit stores (not a register stage's copy), shifts through its own register, generates or computes from, even when a buffer instance also holds it. Judge from port names which instance ports carry relayed data and which a computed result, and say so. The relayed-data sentences above never bar a port of a bus whose address this unit drives on a non-record output port of its own and whose acknowledge it takes on a non-record input port of its own (judge from port names which ports are that bus's address, acknowledge and other lines, and say so): judge each such port as usual (2.6, 2.7); under a conceptual asset about what crosses that bus, the relayed-data bar still keeps every other element from being primary, but each can be a secondary of those ports (2.7).

- Forwarded transactions (c).
  Scope: Relayed data is data a transfer carries into or out of the unit (data loaded or stored, instruction words fetched, messages received or sent).
  Criteria: (1) no statement of this unit stores it or computes from it; (2) it only moves between unit ports, between a unit port and an instance of another IP, between such instances, through a register stage, or into a statement only mixing it with other values (an OR, a multiplexer).

  Outcome: No element qualifies as primary for a conceptual asset about relayed data, alone or with only the acknowledge and ready lines timing its transfer, even in a unit executing instructions and where 4.2 points at it: Phase 1 does not keep such a concept, so it has no secondary (step 5); under other conceptual assets its elements keep their usual labels.
  Evidence: Judge from port names which instance ports carry relayed data and which a computed result, and say so; judge from port names which ports are that bus's address, acknowledge and other lines, and say so.

P1-07.P1_flat: - Bus handshake copies. A bus response acknowledge only repeating or delaying the bus request strobe, and a bus error flag tied to a constant, are not information of their own, except an acknowledge also gating what a read returns. In a unit passing bus requests from an input bus request port to an output one, a register of one bit, or one bit per requester, not a request waiting for a grant (a rule below), holds no information of its own when every assignment to it (directly or through its next-value signal), apart from clearing or holding it, copies or ORs in only the strobe, lock bit or response error bit of the access in progress, or sets it when a test reading only that access's fields and build-time values holds (a route bit), and the unit reads it only to start, pass on, route, time or end that access, the access it serves or that locked sequence, or to drop words that access fetched: the register only re-times a value the access already carries. It is not a piece of its own, although steps 1 to 4, Build-time values and 4.4 would name it a request, status, lock, select, compare or bypass, and even where another rule judges a decision or held request as usual. A compare or decode reading a register this rule bars, and otherwise only that access's own fields and build-time values, or used only to set such a register, is part of that register (step 3), not a piece of its own. Keep no concept for them and cite none of their lines as held lines, except a line also assigning an element this rule does not bar. Judged as usual: the grant, its select and strobe; an address decode choosing which of several output bus request ports gets the access; a pending fence or flush clearing what the unit stores; a busy flag set when the unit itself issues an access; a timeout count, its error and its suppression flag; a reservation; a software-set lock guarding later accesses (not a copied lock bit); a read enable deciding whether stored data leaves on the response; and a cache's hit. A one-bit register that one unconditional statement sets on every clock edge to a stored state bit or flag of this unit, copied or inverted and ANDed only with terms saying when it applies (a request strobe, its read or write bit, an operation-type decode), and that only a bus response's acknowledge or data fields read, only re-times that state to the response. It is part of that state, not a piece of its own, although step 1 names status and responses and step 3 makes a compare of stored state with a request a piece: keep no concept for it and do not cite its lines as held lines. Judged as usual: that state, where held; a register set only from the unit's input ports (a read enable from a strobe and a read or write bit); and a flag that a condition sets to a constant (a timeout error raised at a count's limit).

  Criteria (any of): (1) the acknowledge only repeating or delaying the bus request strobe; (2) the error flag tied to a constant.

  Outcome: are not information of their own.

A compare or decode reading a register this rule bars, and otherwise only that access's own fields and build-time values, or used only to set such a register, is part of that register (step 3), not a piece of its own. - Bus handshake copies (c).
  Scope: A one-bit register.
  Criteria: (1) that one unconditional statement sets on every clock edge to a stored state bit or flag of this unit, copied or inverted and ANDed only with terms saying when it applies (a request strobe, its read or write bit, an operation-type decode); (2) that only a bus response's acknowledge or data fields read.
  Exceptions: that state, where held; a register set only from the unit's input ports (a read enable from a strobe and a read or write bit); and a flag that a condition sets to a constant (a timeout error raised at a count's limit).
